moduleTitle: Recording new steps to resolve bugs in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Insert additional recorded steps into an existing test at a specific position.
Use debugging evidence to investigate missing steps without assuming every failure belongs to the test.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Adding steps to an existing test

elements.term: When a test is missing steps
elements.description: After running a test with debugging, you may find it's lacking some steps, or that some steps are outdated and need re-recording. Rather than re-recording the whole test from scratch, you can add steps manually or record just the missing portion through the AUT.

elements.term: Inserting recorded steps at a position
elements.description: Hover over the arrow between two existing steps where the new steps should go, click Start recording at this position, then record the additional actions on the AUT window — the new steps are inserted exactly where the arrow was, not appended to the end.

elements.term: Start Recording vs. Start recording at this position
elements.description: Testim actually offers two distinct entry points: the plain 'Start Recording'/Record button (available while execution is stopped) appends new steps to the END of the test, while 'Start recording at this position' — triggered from the arrow between two steps — inserts steps at that exact mid-test point instead.

elements.term: Setting up the AUT state before recording mid-test
elements.description: Run to the insertion point with the required AUT state, then record the missing sequence and Stop recording. Review inserted actions and assertions, save and replay the full relevant flow; an insertion alone does not certify the defect is fixed.

bulletPoints: A test lacking steps or with outdated steps doesn't require a full re-record.
Hover the target arrow → Start recording at this position → record just the missing actions in place.
Plain 'Start Recording' = appends to the END of the test; 'Start recording at this position' = inserts at a specific mid-test point.
Run to the target step first (e.g. via manual breakpoint) so the AUT is in the right state before recording — finish with Stop recording.

elements.description: Local breakpoints and stepping expose application state and failed-step evidence. They do not guarantee exact root-cause identification or consistent reproduction of every intermittent failure. Establish whether the missing behavior is in the test, application or environment before adding recorded actions.

bulletPoints: Inspect state and error evidence before choosing a test change.
Replay the revised flow and verify that required assertions still test the intended behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Re-recording an entire test to fix one missing step
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Discarding a whole existing test and re-recording it from scratch because one step sequence in the middle is outdated.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Start recording at this position on the specific arrow where the fix belongs, recording only the missing/updated portion in place — preserving the rest of the test.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test is missing a step in the middle of its flow. What is the recommended way to add it?

options.text: Delete and re-record the entire test from scratch.
Hover the arrow at that position, click Start recording at this position, and record just the missing actions there.
Append the new step to the very end of the test regardless of where it logically belongs.
It isn't possible to insert steps into an existing test.

practiceQuiz.hint: You can insert exactly where needed, not just at the end.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Hovering the arrow between two steps and clicking Start recording at this position inserts newly recorded steps exactly where they're needed, without discarding or re-recording the whole test.

optionExplanations.A: Rebuilding the whole definition is not required for this insertion.
optionExplanations.B: Record at the intended position after establishing the relevant AUT state.
optionExplanations.C: Appending changes the sequence and does not meet the stated middle insertion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What role do breakpoints and step-by-step execution play when resolving a bug in a test?

options.text: They automatically write the missing steps for you.
They expose state and execution evidence that helps investigate the failure before choosing a test change.
They replace the need for recording entirely.
They only work on API validation steps.

practiceQuiz.hint: They're diagnostic tools, not step-writing tools.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Debugging controls help inspect the observed state and steps. They do not automatically write a fix, guarantee reproduction or establish that every defect is a missing test action.

optionExplanations.A: Controls expose execution evidence rather than write the missing actions.
optionExplanations.B: Observed state and steps inform investigation without guaranteeing a diagnosis.
optionExplanations.C: Debug controls do not eliminate recording or manual step editing.
optionExplanations.D: The local debug controls are not API-validation-only.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What's the difference between plain 'Start Recording' and 'Start recording at this position' in Testim?

options.text: They're identical; both always append to the end of the test.
'Start Recording' appends new steps to the END of the test; 'Start recording at this position' inserts them at a specific point via the arrow between two existing steps.
'Start recording at this position' only works on API tests.
'Start Recording' deletes the existing test first.

practiceQuiz.hint: One is end-only; the other lets you pick the exact spot.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Plain 'Start Recording' (available while execution is stopped) appends new steps to the end of the test. 'Start recording at this position', triggered from the arrow between two steps, inserts the new steps exactly at that mid-test point instead.

optionExplanations.A: The two entry points have different insertion locations.
optionExplanations.B: The plain stopped-run Record appends; positioned recording inserts at the arrow.
optionExplanations.C: Positioned recording is not restricted to API tests.
optionExplanations.D: Recording does not automatically delete the definition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before clicking 'Start recording at this position' to fix a bug mid-test, what should you do first to ensure the AUT is in the right state?

options.text: Nothing — no setup step is needed.
Run the test up to the target step (e.g. using a manual breakpoint) so the AUT displays the correct screen state before recording.
Delete all steps after the target position first.
Switch the test to CLI-only mode.

practiceQuiz.hint: Recording blind from the wrong screen state would capture the wrong actions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Running the test up to the target step first — for example via a manual breakpoint — ensures the AUT is actually displaying the correct screen state before you start recording, so the newly recorded actions are the right ones.

optionExplanations.A: The relevant AUT state must be established.
optionExplanations.B: Playback/breakpoint can establish the intended insertion state.
optionExplanations.C: Deleting later steps is not a prerequisite.
optionExplanations.D: CLI-only mode is not required for positioned recording.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you finish a mid-test recording session started with 'Start recording at this position' in Testim?

options.text: Close the browser tab.
Click the Stop recording button.
Wait for an automatic timeout.
Save the test with no specific stop action needed.

practiceQuiz.hint: There's a dedicated button to end the session.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Clicking Stop recording is the explicit action that ends the mid-test recording session and finalizes the newly inserted steps.

optionExplanations.A: Closing the tab is not the documented completion command.
optionExplanations.B: Stop recording ends the recording session.
optionExplanations.C: An automatic timeout is not the documented finish action.
optionExplanations.D: Saving alone does not replace the documented stop-recording action.

quickRecap.value: Start recording at this position adds steps exactly where needed, not from scratch.
Breakpoints/stepping provide evidence for investigation, not a guaranteed exact diagnosis.
Start Recording = end of test; Start recording at this position = a specific mid-test arrow.
Run to the target step (manual breakpoint) so the AUT is in the correct state, then Stop recording to finish.
